fact: Under the PARAE e-government loan, the AfDB finances an artificial intelligence hub and will equip Cote d'Ivoire with AI digital infrastructure, including high-performance computing and GPUs, per AfDB deputy director for West Africa Joseph Ribero.
Minister Djibril Ouattara said on 18 May 2026 that Cote d'Ivoire has begun work on an Ivorian artificial intelligence, with no builder, funder or site named.
The African Development Bank says the national AI strategy unveiled on 13 March 2025 plans an AI laboratory within the Cite de l'innovation et de la culture.

fact: FuturAfric Intelligence Artificielle launched the AI-based YIRI social and e-commerce platform in Abidjan, with six local languages covered, Baoulé and Dioula at 70% progress, and a locally hosted corpus of about 50,000 translated sentences and 300 annotated audio files, per the promoters (Linfodrome).
The director of the Centre national de calcul says the centre will first host Cote d'Ivoire's AI hub and an AI Fab Lab, with startups to get accounts to use the centre's computing remotely.
system: Hub IA and Fab Lab IA at the Centre national de calcul

fact: Led by FuturAfric Artificial Intelligence, the YIRI digital community aims to develop a voice and text language model for Ivorian national languages, backed at its official launch by Minister Djibril Ouattara (Tech Review Africa).

Digital Mag reports that FuturAfric's YIRI project is running the first national campaign to collect and annotate voice and image data in Ivorian languages, training 2,000 young people in 10 regions with 250 trainers, with the aim of building the first Ivorian large language model, not yet released.
The ministry's startup director said an AI Hub will be installed in a renovated and equipped building at the national computing centre CNCCI as a pilot, to move later to VITIB in Grand-Bassam.
